title: refactor(ui): the tool Properties are a label-left property grid
body:
## What changed

![The tool Properties window with the new property grid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/screenshots/pr-2014/tool-properties-window.png)

- The tool Properties page is a label-left property grid: one row per
  setting, label left, input right.
- Four collapsible groups: Geometry, Holder, Cutting data, Catalog.
- New file `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings_grid.rs` holds the grid.
  `tool_settings.rs` loses its long stack of paragraphs.
- The inline help paragraphs are hover tooltips on the row labels.
- The waterjet recipe and the catalog rows use the group header, not a
  nested header.
- Main's #2016 holder-reference display law is kept inside the grid's
  `holder()` rows: holder diameter and length name the library entry
  instead of two typed fields. The merge grafted that law into the grid.

No command changed. Every edit still rides the same Apply / Add commands,
so one edit is one undoable `ChangeTool`.

## Readings

- `docs/decisions/2014-tool-property-grid.md` - what was chosen and dropped.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_properties.rs`: the groups, the
  labels, the label-left order and the fold.
- `layout_page_tool` (in `page_layout.rs`) names the new Geometry header.
- The #2016 pair in `tool_holder_reference.rs` passes on the new grid:
  `a_library_holder_sizes_the_holder_fields_until_its_outline_is_edited`
  and `the_profile_tab_names_the_entry_and_the_picker_shows_it`. The
  picker test hovers the Profile tab before its click: egui hit-tests a
  press with the previous frame, and the grid settles the window size
  over its first frames.
- Structural, edm_tool_visibility, waterjet_recipe and ball_corner tests
  follow the new row layout.

## Gate

- `camcraft-ui` lib tests: 1218 passed, 0 failed, 7 ignored
  (`--test-threads=4`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui`: clean.
- The diff touches `camcraft-ui` only; no other crate's tests apply.

## Not exercised

- Tooltip hover by a real mouse: the structural tests assert labels and
  commands, not hover painting.
- The tool editor window in the theme live lane; it runs only at a cut.

Changelog: The tool Properties show a label-left property grid in four collapsible groups.

Fixes #2014

title: fix(2d): say in a note when the uncut-corner check did not run
body:
## What changed

- `keep_law::narrow_noted` adds a note when the uncut-corner check cannot run.
- The note text is: `<kind>: the check for corners of the stock tighter than the tool did not run (<error>) - look at the stock corners around the part`.
- The log line stays. The path is kept. The note does not block the cut.
- One unit test pins the note.
- `docs/decisions/2511-corner-check-note.md` records the decision.

## Cause

The error arm of the corner check wrote only a `tracing::warn!` line.
The band check directly above it adds a note in the same case.
Thus material could stay in a corner, and the user saw nothing.

## Tests

- Pin: `operation::keep_law::tests::a_corner_check_that_cannot_run_says_so_in_a_note` (`camcraft-app` lib).
- The test is a unit test because `narrow_noted` is `pub(super)`.
- The test uses a tool diameter of 4e12 mm. The erosion returns `GeoError::OutOfRange`, and the two checks fail.
- The test asserts one band note and one corner note. It also asserts that a check that runs adds no "did not run" note.
- Before the fix the pin was red: `the corner check says it did not run: ["2D Pocket: the check for bands of the stock narrower than the tool did not run (coordinates outside the machinable range) - look at the stock around the part"]`, `left: 0`, `right: 1`.
- Mutation: the new `path.notes.push` removed. The pin was red. The line restored. The pin was green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changed.

## Not exercised

- No test gets to the error through the commands or MCP. No legal document makes the corner check fail today.
- No test makes the corner check fail while the band check passes.
- The status line and the UI were not run. They show `Toolpath.notes` as they do for the band note.
- The 0.03 mm noise threshold (`CORNER_HALF_WIDTH`) is not changed. The decision file records the concern of the issue. The review of this number against a measured case stays open work. `Fixes #2511` closes the issue, so that review needs a new issue.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs`.

Changelog: A pocket-family operation that clears the stock around the part now says in a note when its uncut-corner check did not run.

Effort: high

Fixes #2511

title: fix(2d): start a new, larger outline of a whole-model contour at Top Z
body:
## What changed

- A new file, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_whole_reach.rs`, holds `reach_up` and `band_sweep`. When a ring of a deeper band has a tool sweep that reaches outside every sweep cut so far, `reach_up` adds every flat level under Top Z above the ring's first level. Each pass is then at most one stepdown under the pass before it on that ring.
- If the ring cannot be proven clear of the part at the added levels, the operation is refused by name. The toolpath is not made, so nothing posts.
- A ring whose sweep stays inside the cut sweeps is not changed (an outline that does not grow).
- A level at Top Z is never added, because it removes no material.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_whole.rs` keeps the union of the band sweeps (`cover`) and calls `reach_up` after `check_unread`.
- Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2597-new-outline-from-top-z.md`. The stepdown is the axial limit of the operation. So there is no new parameter: its other value would post the buried pass again.

## Readings

- Before the fix, on the #2597 part (boss 30x30 to Z25 on a 60x60 base to Z10, D10, stepdown 5): the base ring was first cut at Z5, 20.000 mm under Top Z 25 (levels `[5.0, 0.0]`).
- Before the fix, on a three-step part: the middle ring was first cut at Z18, 12.000 mm under Top Z 30.
- After the fix: each ring steps down from Top Z in steps of at most the stepdown, and ends at its floor. The depth verifier gives no warning.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `contour_whole_new_outline`:
  - `new_larger_outline_below_top_z_steps_down_from_top_z`
  - `every_new_outline_of_three_steps_steps_down_from_top_z`
  - `an_outline_that_does_not_grow_is_not_walked_again_above`

  The first two fail on main and pass with the fix.
- `camcraft-motion` `contour_whole`: `earlier_blind_hole_stop_does_not_hide_later_counterbore_change` has a changed pin. The upper bore now also has a lap at extent 7 at Z16 and Z12. This is correct: the stock core inside the upper bore grows there. The new helper `assert_bore_laps_at` checks one full lap for each extent and no other move in the bore. All 8 tests pass.
- `camcraft-app` `contour_whole_step`: all 3 tests pass. `case1` caught a `Crossing` warning in the first version, when a level at Top Z was added. The fix leaves out the Top Z level.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 121 steps, 0 failed, 26.8 min.

## Not exercised

- Parts with stock that is narrower than the part's outline. The added passes cut air there (see #2658).
- Tabs on an added level of a new outline. The tab code was not changed.
- A run in the GUI and a real post on a machine.

## Goldens

No CL or NC golden changed. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Shared files

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_whole.rs` is also touched by #2538. This PR does not change `contour_depth.rs`.
- This PR does not touch `tab_bridge.rs` or `contour.rs` (#2561).

## Follow-up

- #2658: start a new outline where the stock starts, not at Top Z.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: Whole-model 2D Contour: a new, larger outline below Top Z is now cut from Top Z down in steps no deeper than the stepdown, or the operation is refused by name. Before, its first pass buried the tool and posted with no warning.

Fixes #2597

title: fix(ui): cache toolpath overlay lines and regions across frames
body:
## What changed

The still-frame cost of the toolpath preview is now cached. On main, an 8114-move Offset path costs the CPU 7.5-10.9 ms on each still frame. The GPU draw is about 0.2-0.3 ms before and after, so the GPU is not the cause.

Main did this work again on every still frame:
- It cloned the path and rebuilt its overlay lines (about 2.6-3.4 ms).
- It measured all solid models again to scale the direction arrows.
- With the operation selected or open on its page, it built the region outline twice.
- The Pocket page note built its own region.
- The operation page and the browser cloned the whole path to read its warnings.

The fix:
- **Path lines** are cached for each operation. The key holds the path signature, the move count, the warnings, the palette, the background colour, the dimming and the arrow size. The arrow size is cached for each model's facets and position. The code moved out of `interact.rs` (1863 to 1797 lines).
- **Region** is kept across frames. The key is the operation value plus `op_stamp`, never `doc_version`. The Pocket page note uses the same cache.
- **No clones**: the new `model::with_toolpath` reads the path without a copy. The operation page and the browser use it.

Main files: `crates/ui/src/path_overlay.rs`, `path_overlay_tests.rs`, `frame_memo.rs`, `egui_app/params_page.rs`, `crates/app/src/model.rs`. Decision entry: `docs/decisions/2201-toolpath-line-cache.md`.

## Readings

CPU time for each still frame (ms), release build, 75 Hz vsync, synthetic 8114-move Offset fixture. Vsync caps the whole frame at about 13.1 ms, so the table sums the CPU timing spans.

| Case | Before | After | Region builds, before / after |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | 2.15 | 1.02 | 0 / 0 |
| shown | 7.50 | 4.46 | 0 / 0 |
| selected | 8.92 | 6.09 | 2 / 0 |
| page | 8.73 | 6.14 | 2 / 0 |
| model source: shown | 8.15 | 4.55 | 0 / 0 |
| model source: selected | 10.88 | 6.06 | 2 / 0 |
| model source: page | 10.80 | 6.67 | 2 / 0 |

Each case is now under the 10 ms target.

## Screenshot

The preview must look the same before and after. The after image is on the `screenshots` branch (commit `4a85a40e5`, `issue-2201/after-preview.png`). It was taken at an earlier head of this branch, before the final commit, and the status bar is cropped. No before image exists: the change is a cache and draws the same lines. The cache tests below compare cached lines with a fresh build.

## Pinning tests

- `path_overlay_tests.rs` (four tests; none pass on main): ten still frames build no lines and measure nothing again; cached lines equal a fresh build; a new path, dimming, palette or model size each cause exactly one rebuild; a hidden path frees its cache entry.
- `selection_frame_cost.rs`: the still-frame pin now expects 0 region builds. Main builds one for each frame, so it fails on main.

Quick gate: 45 steps, 0 failed. Clippy on `camcraft-ui` and `camcraft-app` is clean.

## Not exercised

- `fig8.camproj` was not opened. All readings come from synthetic fixtures of the same size.
- About 2-3 ms of the scene collection step has no timing span. Overlay vertex copies are the likely cause. Filed as #2653 (P7).

Changelog: The toolpath preview no longer rebuilds its lines and region on every still frame, so a long Offset path draws faster.

Fixes #2201

title: fix(ui): hold the playhead while the stock removal is calculated

## What changed

The playback worker calculates the full stock removal before it publishes a frame (#2181). During this time the viewport shows the uncut stock. The transport clock did not stop. - `crates/ui/src/play_precalc.rs`: new `holds_playhead` (true while `Precalc::Running`) and `advance_playhead` (the transport clock step; it does nothing while the calculation runs).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs`: the transport uses `advance_playhead`. The scrub slider is disabled while the calculation runs. Play, Stop and Cancel still work. Cancel stops the calculation, and playback then cuts live as before.
- `crates/app/tests/stock_play_picture.rs` (new): plays the worker as the transport does, composes each frame as the eye does (`max(mesh, cut)`), and counts the solid texels. It proves that the frames show the removal, at the full budget and at the display budget.
- `docs/decisions/2611-playhead-waits-for-precalc.md`: the decision and the dropped options.

## Readings

- Without the fix, the pinning UI test fails: `the playhead waits while the stock removal is calculated`, `left: Some(0.1)`, `right: Some(0.0)`.
- With the fix, it passes (25 s).
- The two app tests pass on main and on this branch. Thus the data of the worker frames is correct, and the defect is the clock.

title: fix(ui): ortho pick rays start at the near plane, not the eye plane
body:
## What changed

PR #1689 moved the orthographic near plane far behind the eye. The ortho eye sits only `ORTHO_EYE_DIST` (100 mm) in front of the target, and the near plane is `(dist * 20).max(1000) - 100` mm behind the eye. But `Camera::ray_through` still started the ortho ray on the eye plane. Thus a face nearer the viewer than the eye plane was drawn, but a click passed it.

Example (the new test): a top view in ortho, and a 300 mm column on Z 0. The view draws the top face at Z 300. Before this change, the click ray started at Z 100, inside the column, and `pick::first_hit_f` found the bottom face at Z 0.

- `crates/ui/src/viewport.rs`:
  - New helper `Camera::ortho_behind_eye()`: the near-plane offset behind the eye plane, in mm.
  - `Camera::mvp` uses it for the ortho `near` (the same value as before).
  - `Camera::ray_through` (ortho branch) moves the origin back by that offset along the view direction. The direction and the line of the ray do not change. The doc comment says so.
- `crates/ui/src/ortho_pick_tests.rs`: two new tests (registered in `lib.rs`).

Why the other ray users are safe (they use the same line, not the old origin point):
- `interact::pick_model` and `feature_click::query_at`: nearest hit along the ray. In ortho the pick radius is one fixed value (`radius_per_depth` is 0), so a farther origin does not change it.
- `move_drag::axis_t`, `turn_drag::plane_angle`: an axis or a plane intersection of the line.
- `box_pick`: the ortho occlusion test uses the view direction.
- The ortho tests in `law_tests.rs` (cursor closure, mode switch, ortho dolly) project points of the ray. In ortho the screen position does not depend on depth.

## Tests

Pinned by (`camcraft-ui` lib, `ortho_pick_tests`):
- `an_ortho_pick_hits_the_top_face_that_stands_above_the_eye_plane`: the click finds `Column` at Z 300.
- `the_ortho_ray_starts_on_the_near_plane_and_keeps_its_line`: for three cursor points the origin is `ortho_behind_eye` behind the eye plane and the rays are parallel; a point on that plane maps to clip depth 0 through `mvp`, so the matrix and the ray agree.

With the old origin (`back = 0`), both tests fail: `the nearest face is the top at Z 300, not [.., 0.0]` and `origin [.., 100.0]`.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, Linux, 12 cores, another build running on the box):
- `ui build (--no-run)`: ok.
- `ui suites: lib`: 1204 passed, 0 failed (both new tests included).
- `ui suites: catalog_render`, `ui suites: gpu_render`: ok.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No click in the running app. The tests use the same two calls as `interact::pick_model` (`Camera::ray_through`, then `pick::first_hit_f`).
- Perspective picking does not change.

## Notes

- `viewport.rs` is already longer than 400 lines. The change adds 9 lines net (+16, -7), of which 7 are the helper and its doc. The tests are in a new file.
- Branch base: `upstream/main`. No context scout ran; this session did its own searches.

title: feat(model): a linked model is imported again when its source file changes
body:
Stacked on #2542 (#2462): review the second commit, `feat(model): a linked model is imported again when its source file changes`. This PR goes back to `main` alone when #2542 merges.

## What changed

- **A model records its source file.** An import from a file records the path and the file's SHA-256 (`schema::ModelSource`, `crates/app/src/model_source.rs`). The record rides `ImportModel`, `UpdateModel` (traded with the facets; undo restores it; a repair keeps it), `DeleteEntity` and `ImportFixture`. A mesh handed in, a browser pick and a generated fixture mesh record none.
- **Project v72.** A model row may have `source: {path, sha256}` (`project/source_dto.rs`). A v71 file steps up unchanged and opens unlinked. A source on a row that is not a model, an empty path, a bad digest or an unknown key is a corrupt file. An older CamCraft refuses a v72 file by name (`unsupported project version 72`).
- **The check** (`crates/ui/src/model_link_watch.rs`). In the window, each linked file is checked about once a second; the frame timer comes back for it while a model is linked. A file is read again only when its size or time moved. A new digest imports the file again through `CommandKind::ImportFile`, and `finish_import` lands a linked file on its model by name. This is the existing re-import: one `UpdateModel`, one undo step, the operations go Stale. **Nothing regenerates or posts.**
- **An undo of that import stays.** The check does not import the same bytes again; only a new change imports.
- **A missing or unreadable file** keeps the model as it is and is said on the status line one time.
- **Unlink.** The Browser's model menu has "Unlink from <file>" (`CommandKind::UnlinkModel`, `SetModelSource`, one undo step). The MCP tool `set_model_link` links (to a path, its digest recorded now, no import) or unlinks (`null`). `get_job` shows `models[].source`.
- **SHA-256** is the kernel's FIPS 180-4 code, re-exported as `camcraft_geometry::solidcraft::sha256_hex` (native only). No new crate dependency.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/2463-linked-model.md`.

## Readings

Live app, debug build, macOS: `camcraft-ui --mcp-port 7921 bracket.stl` (a 40 x 20 x 10 box).

- Before: `get_job` gives `bracket`, bounds max (40, 20, 10), `source.sha256` `00ee0c922a5b…`.
- The file is written again as a 40 x 20 x 25 box. Seven seconds later: bounds max (40, 20, 25), `source.sha256` `0158db27604b…`. No refusal in the log.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/model_link.rs`:
- `an_import_from_a_file_links_the_model_to_that_file`
- `an_update_trades_the_link_and_undo_restores_it`
- `delete_and_undo_keep_the_link`
- `link_and_unlink_are_one_undo_step_each_and_refuse_by_name`
- `the_project_file_keeps_the_link_and_a_v71_file_opens_unlinked` (also: a v73 file is refused by name)
- `a_malformed_source_row_is_refused_as_corrupt`
- `the_mcp_tool_links_and_unlinks_and_get_job_shows_the_source`

`crates/ui/src/model_link_tests.rs`:
- `a_changed_file_is_imported_again_as_one_undo_step_and_its_operations_only_go_stale` (a generated Face operation goes Stale, no generation starts, undo restores it and stays)
- `a_missing_file_keeps_the_model_and_is_said_one_time`
- `unlink_stops_the_check_and_undo_links_again`

`cargo xtask gate quick` after merging upstream main (da87fa5b5): 887 steps, 0 failed (ui lib suite: 1212 passed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Changes to tests outside this feature

- `crates/app/tests/continuous_4axis_part.rs`: the test imports its model from a file, so the model is now linked and the saved example would carry this machine's absolute path. The test unlinks the model before it saves; the committed example names no file. `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` is written again (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`): only `"version"` changes. Upstream main has the file at version 70 and `PROJECT_VERSION` 71; the strict compare compares `"version"` too, so the test is expected to fail there (not run on main here).
- `crates/app/tests/sketch_project.rs`: `assert_eq!(PROJECT_VERSION, 71)` is now `const { assert!(PROJECT_VERSION >= 71) }`. The DXF profile row still arrives at v71; a later step does not break the test.

## Not exercised

- Windows and Linux: not run. The check uses std file metadata only.
- A window that the operating system reports as occluded does not draw frames (existing behaviour), so the check waits until the window is shown.
- A file renamed or moved away reads as missing; link it again with `set_model_link`. There is no "Link to file…" item in the window yet.

## Why

Solidcraft proposes "Send to CamCraft" (tangency-labs/solidcraft#18936, Solidcraft RFC 0001 phases 1 and 3). Each save in Solidcraft writes the `.sc` file again; with this, CamCraft updates the part after each save.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`: the `set_model_link` row).
Changelog: A model imported from a file is linked to it: when the file changes, the model is imported again (one undo step; its operations go Stale). Unlink from the Browser's model menu (#2463).

title: feat(machine): a machine file names its post, and the Setup page offers it
body:
**What changed**

- A `.mch` file can state `controller.post`, the name of a built-in post. `Machine.post`
  holds it. A file without the key reads as before.
- The reader refuses a value that is not a non-empty string, at `controller.post`
  (`post::machine::post_name`).
- The validator also refuses a name that is not a built-in post, and a post that does not
  serve the machine's kind. The post crate gets the registry as a closure, as the holder
  lookup does (#828), so there is no new crate edge.
- `posting::post_offer` returns `Option<PostOffer>`. It offers the machine's named post
  (`OfferWhy::Machine`) when that post is in the registry, serves the mount, and is not
  the setup's post. Otherwise it gives the kind offer as before (`OfferWhy::Kind`). A
  `.cps` file post is never offered over.
- The Setup page's banner tells which offer it is: "the machine names grblHAL as its post;
  switch to it?" or the kind text as before. The button queues `SelectPostNamed`, so it
  rides undo.
- A mount never changes the post by itself (#343, #388).
- The MCP tools say the same, after the QA finding on #2374. `post_offer_for` asks for any
  setup (`posting_offer.rs`). `load_machine` replies with `post_offer` for the setup that it
  mounted to, and `get_job` gives `post_offer` for each setup: the post, why, and the
  `set_setup_post` call that takes it. `null` means no offer.
- The description of the `post` tool lists every name in `BUILTINS`. The hand-written list
  did not have "Tormach PathPilot", grblHAL, TinyG or the Carvera posts.
- 32 shipped machine files state their post, where `MACHINES`, a machine's issue or its
  post writes the pairing: the PathPilot mills, routers, lathes and plasma table, grblHAL
  and the Sienci AltMills, TinyG, the Makera machines, the Doosan DNM 5700s and the Haas
  machines. The generic machines, the Sodick ALC400G, the Mach3-era Tormach mills and the
  sinker template state none.
- The Machines pane's file editor gives a user's own machine its post. General has a Post
  row, a dropdown (`Field.choices`) of the built-in posts that serve the file's kind, plus
  "(none)", which takes the key out. A stated name off the list stays in view with its
  refusal. Only built-in posts are offered: a `.cps` file has no stable name for a machine
  file to state.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2374-machine-names-its-post.md`.

**Readings**

Branched from `main` at `6349a542e`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 346 steps, 0 failed, on `2d26ef2a3`.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --base upstream/main`: 837 steps, 836 ok, 61.9 min. The one red step was
  `clippy -D warnings` (`bool::then` with a closure in `posting_offer.rs`), fixed in
  `a9205467b`; that step reran green with `--failed`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head `b6bc94239`, clean tree: green,
  346 steps, 0 failed, 10.0 min.
- By hand, the release build: a setup on the grblHAL machine is offered the grblHAL post
  and the switch rides undo; a user's own machine picks its post from the editor's dropdown,
  writes it, and the Setup page then offers it.

**Pinning tests**

- `crates/app/tests/machine_library.rs`:
  `a_machine_that_names_its_post_is_offered_it_and_the_choice_rides_undo`,
  `the_named_post_must_be_a_built_in_post_that_serves_the_machine`,
  `the_editor_offers_the_built_in_posts_that_serve_the_machine`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machine_named_post.rs`:
  `the_grblhal_machine_offers_its_own_post_and_the_switch_rides_undo`,
  `a_users_own_machine_picks_its_post_from_the_editors_dropdown`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_machine_post.rs`:
  `mounting_the_770mx_offers_pathpilot_and_the_agent_takes_it_as_one_undo_step`,
  `the_offer_follows_the_setup_the_machine_went_to_not_the_active_one`,
  `a_machine_that_names_no_post_and_serves_the_current_one_offers_nothing`,
  `the_post_tool_lists_every_registry_post`
- `crates/post/src/machine/post_name.rs`: five unit tests for the reader and the rule.
- Not changed and still green: the lathe-over-mill-post offer test in
  `ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs`, `plasma_post.rs` (only moved to `offer.post`) and
  `sinker_burn.rs`.

**Not exercised**

- By hand: a `.cps` file post on the setup is not offered over. The tests pin it.
- An older reader on a new file. `Machine` is `#[serde(default)]`, so an older reader drops
  the key and loses only the offer, never a posted line. Thus no `PROJECT_VERSION` bump.

  does not change for them.
- An MCP agent on a document without setups. The `set_setup_post` refusal names
  `select_post`, which is not an MCP tool; the offer's hint says `add_setup`, then
  `set_setup_post`. The refusal text did not change here.

body:
## What changed

A post script for Grbl 1.1 3-axis mills, and a machine for it.

- `assets/posts/grbl.cps` (new). Derived from our `grblhal.cps`. Grbl 1.1 has no canned cycles, no cutter radius compensation and no tool table, so:
  - Drill cycles post as G0/G1/G4 moves. The engine already sends the expanded hole moves, and the script passes them through (as `tinyg.cps` does). A dwell (P > 0) is a G4 at the hole bottom.
  - BORE and TAP are refused by name. An expanded bore needs a spindle stop before the rapid retract; a tap needs a synchronised spindle.
  - A tool change is a retract, a comment `(TOOL CHANGE - LOAD T<n> - SET Z ZERO - RESUME)` and `M0`. The first tool gets `(LOAD T<n> AND SET Z ZERO BEFORE THE START)`. No M6, no G43/G49.
  - G41/G42 control compensation is refused, as on TinyG.
  - A line is at most 79 characters (the Grbl 1.1 line buffer is 80 bytes with the terminator). A comment is cut to fit. A motion line that does not fit refuses the program.
- `assets/machines/grbl-3axis.mch` (new): a copy of `grblhal-3axis.mch`, model "Grbl 3-axis".
- `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`: the post "Grbl 1.1" after TinyG, the machine "Grbl 3-axis", and their embedded copies.

body:
**Stacked on #2342** (`issue/796-tormach-wrapped-a`, Fixes #796). This branch starts from that PR's head `ef864e37d`; until #2342 merges, this PR's diff also shows its files. It merges after #2342. Fork synced at upstream main 4e8616b (through #2342's branch).

## What changed

The continuous half of #1904: a step-by-step guide page for the Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, with a committed demo project and drawn pictures.

- **Page:** `site/content/guide/getting-started/first-continuous-4axis-part.md`, "Your first continuous 4-axis program". It covers: how the bar is held; the machine file's four A values (axis, travel, `nose_to_axis`, A rate) and what to compare with the machine; finding the A centreline and setting G54 on it; the ball tool; a Rotary Parallel operation, setting by setting; the checks and what the stock simulation says; the posted program read line by line; what the post refuses; a run in the PathPilot simulator; then a single-block start and an air cut with no bar.
- **What the post writes, in plain words, from the Hub readings on #796:** `G93` on a feed that turns A with X Y Z, and why (reading 2: in `G94` F is the X Y Z distance only; reading 3: `G93` is accepted and timed); the A rate cap worked out on real lines; an A-only feed in `G94` with F in degrees per minute (reading 4); A counting on through 180 (reading 1); `G94` back before the last rapid.
- **Demo project:** `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj`, the program it posts `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc` (3213 lines) and the model `examples/models/first-continuous-4axis-part.obj` (made by `gen_first_continuous_4axis_part_obj.py`). #2342's kit project was not reused: it has no continuous operation, and its wrap golden has a stock that ends where the model ends.
- **Pictures:** three SVG files in `site/static/guide-pictures/`, drawn from the committed project, model and program by `site/tools/first_continuous_4axis_pictures.py`: the bar and the work offset, each move unrolled (X against A), and the A word line by line with the G93 lines marked. No PNG, no screenshot. The UI renderer of #1902 (PR #2078) is not merged, so there are no UI renders yet.
- **Links and corrections:** linked from Getting started, First run, "Your first 4-axis part", the Multi-axis index and "Continuous 4-axis". `continuous-4-axis.md` no longer says that no shipped post writes inverse-time feed, and the Multi-axis index no longer says that `tormach.cps` indexes A only (both untrue since #2342). `continuous-4-axis.md` has a new section "End faces and the chuck".
- `docs/decisions/1904-continuous-4axis-walkthrough.md`.

## Two findings that shape the page

1. **The page ends with an air cut and tells the reader not to cut.** Rotary Parallel finishes both end faces of the model down to the axis. On a bar held in a chuck, the chuck-side end face is inside the bar: the program feeds to Z-0.03 at X-1.3125 while the stock goes on to X-2. With a 1/2 in flute the shank check blocks the post (good); with a longer flute it posts with no warning. No setting keeps the pass off an end face. Filed as **#2343**. The page says this at the top, in "Check it" and at the end.
2. **The shipped machine leaves A travel unstated.** Rotary Offset can count past one turn on this machine file. A custom machine with bounded A travel can refuse that count. Filed as **#2344**.

This is a partial delivery for #1904. The wrapped engraving or slot is unavailable. Neither program has a recorded PathPilot Hub run to M30. The guide describes an air cut, but no Hub run or machine run was done. Keep #1904 open for this acceptance work.

Inherited parent #2342 head `b93fe06131248f91e41e90104e0d050409add852` with a merge commit. Its feed-time calculation bounds the curved part-relative trajectory from the rounded posted words. The parent includes an independent trajectory pin. This child refreshes its example program for that safety correction. The guide now explains the curved trajectory bound. Both NC comparisons allow tightly bounded platform rounding differences. The comparisons preserve line structure and exact nonnumeric words. The independent rate checks remain. The committed program refresh is required by the inherited safety fix, rather than used to hide platform differences.

body:
## What changed

A new built-in post **LinuxCNC** (`assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`, extension `.ngc`) and a generic machine **LinuxCNC 3-axis** (`assets/machines/linuxcnc-3axis.mch`). The post uses the RS274NGC dialect from the public LinuxCNC 2.9 G-code and M-code references. Its structure comes from our own `tormach.cps`. The PathPilot assumptions are removed: no "machine Z0 is the top" convention, no G30 before each tool change, no belt-range notes, no 1-1000 tool range, no 4th axis.

Post options (declared, so the UI, CLI and MCP show them):

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `retractMode` | `g53` (`G53 G0 Z<safe_retract>`), `g28` / `g30` (`G91 G28 Z0` + `G90`, Z only), `none` | `g53` |
| `writeToolLength` | `G43 H<n>` after `T<n> M6`; off when the M6 remap applies the length (the section `G49` is then left out too) | on |
| `pathControl` / `blendTolerance` | `G64 P<tol>` (mm, written in the program unit) or `G61` | `G64 P0.025` |
| `programEnd` | `M30` or `M2` | `M30` |
| `percentDelimiters` | `%` on the first and the last line | off |

Also: safe start block `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G49 G80`, no O word, comments in parentheses (active keywords made inert), `S M3`, `M7`/`M8`/`M9` from the machine coolant list (`PARAM Coolant` read), arcs and helices with incremental IJK (or the R-arc option), G73/G81/G82/G83/G85/G86/G89 with G99, G38.2/G38.3 probing as in the PathPilot post.

Dwell words (as main's fixes on `tormach.cps` and `grblhal.cps`): each opening `G86` block has a P word (`P0` for no dwell, #2362). A back-bore with no dwell posts `G85`, not a `G89` with no P (#2360). A `G83` dwell is refused by name (#2348). Pinned by `bore_cycle`, `dwell_cycles_modal_p` and `g83_dwell_linuxcnc` (`crates/post/tests/`).

Base: upstream main `fac6c8e8d` (not a cut tag: the fork main is behind v0.22.0, and this PR targets upstream main).

Tapping:
- A rigid tap is `G33.1 Z<bottom> K<pitch>` (pitch = feed / rpm). The post writes it only when the machine file states `rigid_tapping: true` (the reference requires a spindle encoder). Else it refuses by name.
- A floating-holder tap is `G84 ... F<rpm x pitch>` (the reference says G84 is not spindle-synchronized). The post declares `floatingTapping = true`.

Refused by name: `G53` retract with no stated `safe_retract` (no machine included, #435 / #495), control compensation (G41/G42), tilted moves, a trip home after an operation, tool numbers that are not positive whole numbers, G73/G83 with Q <= 0.

Engine: the machine mirror read an unstated `rigid_tapping` as `rigidTapping: true` (the unstated-limit law). The post must not take that as "an encoder is present". So the engine now also publishes `machine.rigidTappingStated` (true only for a stated `rigid_tapping: true`). No other post reads it. `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents it.

Registration: `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES` (`crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`), the post-name lists in `cam.d.ts` and `script/mod.rs`, README, `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`. Decisions: `docs/decisions/2303-linuxcnc-post.md`.

## How it was tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/linuxcnc_post.rs` (9 tests): registry and library; unstated safe Z refused, never `G53 G0 Z0`; stated safe Z before `M6`, after `G43` and at the end; `G28`/`G30`/none retracts; no `G43`/section `G49` with the remap option; `G61`, `M2`, `%`, inch blend tolerance, end units; rigid tap refused without an encoder and `G33.1 Z-12 K1.5` with one (inch `K0.059055`); floating tap `G84`; tilted move and control compensation refused. Every program is checked to hold only G/M words from the LinuxCNC reference.
- `conformance`: new goldens `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/linuxcnc/*.nc` (12) and `synth_linuxcnc.nc`; `tap_plate` is a named refusal on the generic VMC (no encoder stated); extension `.ngc` pinned.
- `script_linuxcnc` (post binary on the recorded streams, goldens in `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/linuxcnc/`). These are machine-less, so each case is the named safe-Z refusal (or the 3-axis refusal).
- Cross-post lists extended: `cycle_hop` (hop law, run with `retractMode=g30`), `ream_cycle`, `comp`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post_spindle_rule_all`, `machine`.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, head 95b83ca24, macOS): 579 steps, 573 green. The 6 red suites are exactly the 18 tests that #2306 lists as red on this base (`fac6c8e8d`, main is red after batch 16): `circular_pick_law`, `keep_law`, `kept_parts_live`, `pocket3d_open_side`, `stock_source_holes`, `trochoid_law`. None of them posts through this post.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` and clippy on the new and changed app test targets: clean.

## Not exercised

- Not run in a LinuxCNC sim or on a machine. The reporter (sn3ro) offered a LinuxCNC 2.9 sim run and an air cut.
- G33.1 and G84 behaviour on a real spindle; the `none` retract with a real M6 remap.
- Control compensation (G41/G42) is refused, not written. A 4th axis is not supported.

title: feat(app)!: place a DXF profile on a setup's stock - Sketch entity, ImportDxf, import_dxf MCP tool
body:
Stacked on #2106 (sketch chaining, issue 1861). Merge #2106 first. This branch now merges upstream `main` and keeps both project modules and the breakthrough fields from #1557.

## What changed

A DXF drawing is now a profile that the user places on the stock of a setup. It is not a model. This follows the scope change of the maintainer on issue 1862 (2026-11-15).

- **`Sketch` component** (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`, registered in `register_schema`). It holds the setup and the shared drawing data. The entity has no `Facets`, and `model::is_model` is false for it. No 3D solid tool reads it as a mesh.
- **`camcraft_geometry::sketch_data::SketchData`**: the primitives in mm, the layer names, the source units, the join tolerance, the chains of issue 1861 and the import summary. The chains are always made from the stored primitives.
- **Placement** (`crates/app/src/sketch.rs`): the `Location` of a profile is relative to the top face of the stock of its setup, at the stock origin. A profile has Z 0 and a turn about the face normal only. A moved or resized stock carries the profile.
- **`ImportDxf::new(world, setup, path, options)`** (undoable). It gets the setup as an argument (`None`: the active setup). It refuses at construction: a setup with no stock, an unknown setup, a file that is not `.dxf`, a malformed DXF, a drawing with nothing to place, a name in use. A file with no `$INSUNITS` (absent or 0) and no unit from the caller gives the typed `CommandError::DxfUnitsMissing { width, height }`.
- **`MoveSketch::new(world, name, x, y, angle_deg)`** (undoable): the move and the turn on the stock face.
- **`DeleteEntity`** restores a profile on undo. **`SelectEntity`** works on a profile. **`MoveModel`** and **`DeleteSetup`** refuse a profile by name.
- **Virtual model reference** (`crates/app/src/sketch_model.rs`): it is derived from the world when a setup has a placed profile and the document has no part. Nothing is stored for it.
- **Project file**: entity kind `sketch` with a `sketch` key; `PROJECT_VERSION` 70 -> 71. The chains are made again on load.
- **MCP**: `import_dxf` and `move_dxf_profile`. `get_job` lists `profiles`, gives each setup a `model_reference`, and gives an operation on a profile `checks_against`. **Script**: `cam.importDxf(path, { setup, units, join_tol, name })`.
- `docs/decisions/1862-sketch-profile.md` records the design of the virtual reference: what it is in the ECS, what the project file stores, and which checks read it.

## How each point of the scope change is met

1. A profile is not a model: `is_model` is false, `model_entities` does not list it, `get_job` lists it under `profiles`.
2. A setup with a stock and no model is legal: the tests make a sheet stock, place the profile and add an operation.
3. The `Sketch` belongs to the setup. Its `Location` is relative to the stock top face at the stock origin. `MoveSketch` moves and turns it on that face.
4. `ImportDxf` gets the setup. Undo removes the profile. The MCP tool and the script verb get the same argument.
5. The virtual model reference is `sketch_model::of(world, setup)`. The source door of the operation commands accepts a profile as a source. The model-height diagnostic names the reference. `sketch_model::model_loaded` is the question for the operation pages of issue 1863. The reference has no facets.
6. No check passes silently. An operation on a profile states what it is checked against (the stock and the chains of the profile). A kind that needs a solid model refuses a profile by name. A 3D kind in a setup with a virtual reference refuses by name. Generation of an operation on a profile refuses by name (see the open questions).
7. The decision file is in this PR.

## Project file version

This PR writes **version 71**. Current upstream `main` writes version 70 (v67 WCS flip #1720, v68 drill break-through #2441, v69 2D Adaptive #1517, v70 holder reference #2016). Profiles take the next version. The v70-to-v71 profile step needs no data rewrite. The text that follows in this paragraph is from the earlier head: read each "v67" in it as "v71". Main's trunnion fields, v65-to-v66 migration and earlier steps stay intact, and the v66-to-v67 profile step needs no data rewrite. Stated `controller_rtcp: false` and trunnion data remain intact, as do tilt bases, earlier cutting-data rows and breakthrough values. A v62 file still loads through the earlier migration (`a_v62_file_steps_up_unchanged`). Tests check v63 breakthrough and v64 cutting-data files through load, save as v67, and load again. The v65 tilt pins retain legacy basis 0 and basis 1 through load, save, and reload. The new v66 trunnion pin checks the stated machine data through load, save, and reload. The profile and rest payloads also survive a v67 save and load.

## Open design questions

These need a decision of the maintainer. This PR does the part that is specified and does not guess the rest.

1. **Toolpath from the chains.** The added "Done means" says that the setup "accepts a 2D operation on the sketch chains". This PR accepts the operation at each command door (create, paste, retarget, retype, move to a setup). It does not generate a toolpath from the chains: issue 1864 has that work (chain picks, side per chain, checks without a mesh). Until then, generation refuses by name and says what the operation is checked against. Is that the correct split, or must #1862 also generate?
2. **Top of Model and Bottom of Model on a virtual reference.** A reference with no solid has no top and no bottom. This PR refuses these heights by name (the text tells the user to use a stock or fixed height). The alternative is to give them a value, for example the stock top and the stock bottom. That changes cut depths, so it is not decided here.
3. **"The stock origin".** This PR reads it as the origin of the stock entity. For a box and a cylinder that is the centre in XY. The alternative is a corner of the stock or the WCS origin.
4. **Which kinds take a profile.** This PR admits the 2D milling, plasma and wire EDM sections. Drilling (holes from DXF circles), turning and sinker EDM refuse a profile by name. Is that the correct set?
5. **`MoveSketch` and not `MoveModel`.** The issue body said `MoveModel`. A profile has a face placement (X, Y, angle), and `MoveModel` writes a world placement and carries the stock. This PR adds `MoveSketch`, and `MoveModel` refuses a profile by name.
6. **A profile that is larger than the stock, or off its edge,** is not refused at placement. Issue 1864 has the check of the chains against the stock.

## Pinning tests

`crates/geometry/tests/sketch_data.rs` (9): units and scale, the missing-units refusal with extents, an unsupported unit code, an empty drawing, stored parts read back, arc bounds, and invalid stored summary counts.

`crates/app/tests/sketch_profile.rs` (8):
- `a_dxf_profile_lands_on_the_stock_top_at_the_stock_origin_and_is_not_a_model` (the placement on the stock top)
- `a_profile_moves_and_turns_on_its_stock_face_with_undo_and_redo` (the move on the stock, undo and redo)
- `a_file_without_units_is_the_typed_missing_units_error_until_a_unit_is_stated`
- `an_import_that_cannot_stand_is_refused_at_construction`
- `a_stock_and_profile_setup_accepts_a_2d_operation_and_refuses_what_needs_a_solid` (the two refusals, the generation refusal)
- `a_profile_belongs_to_its_setup_and_deleting_it_is_undoable`
- `deleting_the_entity_frees_its_drawing`
- `stock_source_word_is_reserved_for_explicit_profile_names_and_file_stems`

`crates/app/tests/sketch_project.rs` (14):
- `a_stock_and_profile_setup_saves_and_loads_with_its_2d_operation` checks the profile and its operation through a version-71 save and load.
- `rest_parameters_and_profile_rows_share_the_v71_project_file` checks both payloads in the version-71 file.
- `a_v63_break_through_file_steps_up_without_losing_the_stated_limit` checks that a version-63 breakthrough limit survives migration, save, and load.
- `a_v62_file_steps_up_unchanged` checks the earlier format migration.

`crates/app/tests/mcp_dxf.rs` (2): `import_dxf_places_a_profile_and_states_units_and_skipped_counts`, `a_profile_moves_on_the_stock_and_takes_a_2d_operation_but_no_3d_one` (MCP, save and reopen, and the script verb).

`crates/app/tests/tilt_basis_compat.rs` (7): five inherited compatibility pins and two new v65 load/save/reload pins:

- `a_v65_legacy_tilt_steps_up_without_changing_its_basis` preserves the legacy basis and A 30 / B 20 degrees.
- `a_v65_basis_one_tilt_steps_up_without_losing_its_stated_basis` preserves basis 1 and A 30 / B 20 degrees.

## Trunnion compatibility refresh

Takeover refresh (2026-11-18): the current head is `030ba52d021ae24a1eda448f29cfe9b837726455`. It merges upstream main at `e7f5f43159459f0e64e42dd317f06b769d8a1e51`. Profiles write v71 after v70 of main. The takeover comment has the conflicts, the hand edits and the tests of this head. The sections below are the history of the earlier heads; their "v67" is the old number.

Current head: `e0abb5eca7a79c50a5b20ecd72f94165b49b6217`. Merged upstream main `fac6c8e8d22cb39bb0a4c18644b4ec1c4dbd2db6` and kept its trunnion fields, format history, migrations and MCP additions. Profiles write v67 after main's v66.

- `a_v66_trunnion_steps_up_without_losing_its_stated_rtcp_and_kinematics` preserves `controller_rtcp: false`, rotary chain order, pivots, offsets, zero offsets, rollover and sign convention through load, save as v67 and reload. The full saved document changes only its version. Post properties retain RTCP false.
- Both mutations were RED: changing PROJECT_VERSION back to 66, and omitting controller_rtcp from serialization. Restoring each fix was GREEN.
- All 114 targeted tests passed across trunnion_schema, sketch_project, tilt_basis_compat, break_through, sketch_profile, mcp_dxf and project_roundtrip. Both v65 tilt pins remain.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` selected batch and finished RED: 804 steps, 7 failed; 7,450 tests passed, 19 failed, 67 ignored. Failed suites: `circular_pick_law`, `keep_law`, `kept_parts_live`, `pocket3d_open_side`, `stock_source_holes`, `trochoid_law`, and the UI library's rest-pocket Zigzag refusal test. All requested format pins passed inside the gate.

title: feat(ai): provider HTTP clients, keychain keys and offline-only mode
body:
**New third-party crates - needs the maintainer's decision (`needs-maintainer`):**

| Crate | Version | Licence | Why the workspace's existing deps can't do it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reqwest` | 0.12.28 (default features off, `rustls-tls`) | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | Provides an async HTTP request that cancellation can interrupt. Redirects and environment proxies are disabled. |
| `tokio` | 1.52.3 (`rt`, `time`, `net`, `macros`) | MIT | Runs each request on a current-thread runtime inside the chat worker. Cancellation drops the active request future. |
| `rustls` / `rustls-webpki` / `rustls-pki-types` | 0.23.46 / 0.103.17 / 1.16.0 (via reqwest) | Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT / ISC / MIT OR Apache-2.0 | TLS for the https cloud APIs; no OpenSSL on Linux. |
| `ring` + `untrusted` | 0.17.14 / 0.9.0 (via rustls) | Apache-2.0 AND ISC / ISC | rustls's crypto (C/asm, built by `cc`; no CMake, unlike aws-lc-rs). |
| `webpki-roots` | 1.0.12 | CDLA-Permissive-2.0 | The Mozilla CA roots, so the build needs no system trust store. |
| `keyring` + `keyring-core` | 4.2.0 / 1.0.1 | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | Nothing in the tree reaches an OS credential store. |
| keyring stores: `apple-native-keyring-store` (+ `security-framework`), `windows-native-keyring-store`, `zbus-secret-service-keyring-store` (+ `secret-service`) | 1.x | MIT OR Apache-2.0 | macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Secret Service. The Linux store rides the `zbus` 5 **already in the lock** - pure Rust, no `libdbus` build package. |
| RustCrypto `aes`, `cbc`, `cipher`, `hkdf`, `hmac`, `sha2`, `digest`, `subtle`, `zeroize`, ... (via secret-service) | various | MIT OR Apache-2.0 (`subtle` BSD-3-Clause) | Secret Service session encryption. |

`url` 2.5 was **already in Cargo.lock** and is now a direct dependency of `camcraft-app` (endpoint parsing with the same URL parser reqwest uses). All new crates are under `[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]` of `camcraft-app` only; the browser build links none of them. Notices added to `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`. The review fix replaces blocking `ureq` with `reqwest` and a current-thread `tokio` runtime so cancellation interrupts active requests. Considered and dropped: detached blocking requests (they keep the socket and worker alive), `native-tls` (OpenSSL headers on Linux), keyring's dbus store (vendored libdbus C build) - see `docs/decisions/1945-ai-provider-clients.md`.

## What changed

- **`camcraft_app::ai`** (new, `crates/app/src/ai/`):
  - `endpoint` - URL parse (WHATWG `url`; user info, query and fragment refused), loopback test (`localhost`, 127/8, `::1`, IPv4-mapped), `admit` (offline-only reaches loopback alone; plain `http://` off the machine is refused, key or not), `admit_addrs` (the resolver's half).
  - `presets` - Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (GPT and Codex), Gemini `generateContent` (all `https://`); Ollama `http://localhost:11434/v1`, Unsloth Studio `http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`, LM Studio `http://localhost:1234/v1`, llama.cpp `llama-server` `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` (`--jinja` named in the label).
  - `wire` - the request path and body per provider. Tool-call envelopes are echoed in each provider's own shape (Anthropic content blocks, Chat `tool_calls` message, Responses `output` items incl. reasoning, Gemini content incl. `thoughtSignature`); consecutive tool results merge into one Anthropic user message / one Gemini turn. Model ids are checked so they cannot add a query or climb the Gemini path. Fallback (prompt-JSON / Q&A) payloads go into the system prompt with no tools.
  - `probe` - Ollama `/api/show` capabilities -> tools / vision / fallback mode.
  - `secret` - `ApiKey` has no `Display` and a redacted `Debug`, refuses control characters (no header injection); lookup is the env var (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`) first, then the keychain.
  - `http` (native only) - the client. `admit` runs before anything resolves; the agent's resolver refuses non-loopback addresses when offline-only or plain http; **no redirects followed**, **no proxy from the environment**, connect/total timeouts, auth only in headers (`x-api-key`, `Authorization: Bearer`, `x-goog-api-key`), errors carry the host, status and the provider's message - never the key.
  - `keychain` (native only) - `load` / `store` / `forget` under the service `camcraft-ai`.
- **`prefs.json`** gains `aiOfflineOnly` (written only when on); `ViewPrefs` has no field that could hold a key.
- **AI Chat dock** (`crates/ui`): native builds use the new `transport_http::HttpTransport` (presets map to the endpoints above; the key comes from env/keychain or the step is refused by name; an Ollama model without the `tools` capability is refused by name in the native-tools preset, pointing at the Prompt-JSON / Q&A presets). The "Offline only" switch is restored from and saved to `prefs.json`. The browser build keeps the offline-only `DefaultTransport` (now `cfg(wasm32)`).

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/ai_http.rs` against a fake loopback HTTP server (no real key: a fixed placeholder sent only to 127.0.0.1): `anthropic_messages_wire_format`, `openai_chat_completions_wire_format`, `openai_responses_wire_format`, `gemini_generate_content_wire_format`, `local_runtimes_send_no_auth_header`, `ollama_capability_probe`, `offline_only_blocks_every_non_loopback_host_before_a_socket` (every cloud preset plus TEST-NET / private / IPv6 hosts refused in < 500 ms, plus the resolver check), `plain_http_off_this_machine_is_refused`, `redirects_are_not_followed_and_errors_never_carry_the_key`. 9/9 pass.
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs::offline_only_survives_and_the_file_stores_zero_keys` (the file's keys are exactly the known five; no "key"/"token"/"secret"/"password"/"bearer").
- Unit tests in `ai::endpoint`, `ai::presets`, `ai::secret`, `ai::wire`, `ai::probe`, and `transport_http::every_panel_preset_has_an_endpoint`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (fell back to batch: Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock changed): geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app (incl. `ai_http`, `view_prefs`) and ui suites all **ok** (35.5 min). Clippy `-D warnings` FAILS only on `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs:115` `MIN_LABEL_PX` never used - pre-existing on upstream main since PR #2095, tracked in #2104 / PR #2111; no other lint in the touched crates.
- `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (with `web/build-app-wasm.sh`'s wasi sysroot and flecs patch): **Finished** clean; the only warnings are pre-existing unused imports in `ai_chat/worker.rs` (untouched here).

## Not exercised

- No call to a real provider or a real local runtime (no key in tests, no network in tests).
- The OS keychain itself (`keychain::load/store/forget`) is not called by any test - a test would prompt or write the developer's real keychain; the lookup order is pinned with an injected keychain.
- No UI for entering/storing a key yet: keys come from the env vars, or from the keychain if stored by other means (service `camcraft-ai`, account `anthropic`/`openai`/`gemini`). A key-entry field is a follow-up.
- Streaming responses (each step is one complete response, as the dock's worker expects).

title: fix(fidelity): a stock copy of an incomplete model keeps naming its hole
body:
A stock copied from an incomplete model (#1610) now keeps naming that model's hole after the model is deleted. Before this change, its refusal at the post fell back to "saved before CamCraft recorded mesh fidelity (project v58 or older)". The post still refused it; only the reason given was wrong.

Fixes #1700

## What changed

The copy's refusal read the hole from the source model by name (`mesh_open::unknown_note`), so once the source was gone the lookup found nothing. Now the copy carries the hole itself (`schema::MeshOpen`), beside the fidelity-unknown sentinel it already carried (#1056):

- **Where the hole is copied:** every place that lands the sentinel on a copy now lands the hole with it:
  - `SetStock` and its undo
  - a setup clone (`CreateSetup` with a datum)
  - an undone `DeleteSetup`
  - `UpdateModel`'s refresh of the copies, and its undo
  - the project loader
- **Where the refusal reads it:** `model_fidelity::op_problem` reads the hole off the entity that carries the sentinel. Two small helpers: `mesh_open::hole_behind` (the twin of `model_fidelity::chord_behind`) and `mesh_open::note_for`.
- **Project file:** the saver already wrote `mesh_open` for any entity that has one. The loader now also accepts it on a `FromModel` stock marked `fidelity_unknown`, and a hole without the mark stays corrupt. There is no version bump: #1610's check (a hole on anything but a model is corrupt) has not shipped in a cut yet, so no released reader refuses these files.

The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/1700-stock-copy-hole.md`.

## How tested

- **New:** `crates/app/tests/stock_copy_hole.rs` (6 tests). A copy carries the hole, and its refusal names the source and the hole:
  - after the source is deleted, and across undo and redo of that delete;
  - after save, load, and a second save that matches byte for byte;
  - through a setup clone and an undone setup delete;
  - through a whole re-import of the source (which clears it) and that re-import's undo;
  - through `SetStock`'s undo.

  The file also checks that a stock with a hole and no mark fails to load as corrupt.
- **Without the fix,** the two "source deleted" tests fail: the refusal reads "saved before CamCraft recorded …".
- **Existing tests:** the `import_step_open_shell` tests from #1610 still pass. Its corrupt-file message check passes too, because the new message keeps the old wording as a prefix.
- **Gate:** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green (112 app suites), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branched from upstream/main after #1699 merged, not from a cut tag: the code this fixes is not in v0.20.0.

title: fix(post): Tormach lathe G76 J makes LinuxCNC's R1 ladder cut the record's passes
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`, `g76Grid`: J (first depth) is no longer floored to the grid on its own. LinuxCNC's G76 with `R1` cuts J, 2J, ... with the last pass clamped at K, so the control cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The record lays n = ceil(height / first depth) equal rungs (g76Why already holds the equal ladder), so J must satisfy (n-1)J < K <= nJ:

- J is the shallower grid rounding (as before) when that keeps the count;
- when the shallower J would add a pass, J is the one grid step up, and never a full grid step over the record's first cut;
- otherwise the record is refused by name: `G76 threading cycle refused - no first depth J on the control's grid makes R1's equal ladder cut the record's n passes (K ...)`.

The root keeps its outward rounding. Peak, root, I and K are unchanged.

## Golden change, line by line

`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc`, one line:

```
-G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0314 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
+G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0315 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
```

What this relies on, from the public LinuxCNC G-code reference (G76): J is the first cut depth, K the full thread depth (diameters here, under G7), and `R1.0` selects constant depth, so each pass goes J deeper than the last and the last pass is clamped at K.
- Old: 0.0314, 0.0628, 0.0942, then 0.0944 (a 0.0002 in pass) = 4 passes. The record laid and the verdict judged 3 (0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 mm radius).
- New: 0.0315, 0.0630, 0.0944 (clamped) = 3 passes, the record's count. J 0.0315 in is 0.000004 in (0.1 um) over the record's Ø0.8 mm first cut. The root (X + I - K) is the same as before: never deeper than the minor.
- P, Z, I, K, R, Q, H and every other line are unchanged. The mm golden (`J0.8 K2.4`) is byte-identical.

The earlier PathPilot Hub 8L sim run of this golden (PR #517 comments) does not cover the new J: **this golden needs a new Hub run** (not done here, no Hub access).

Scan (local script, not committed): realistic records (first depth 0.05-0.5 mm, height 0.3-2 mm, four minor diameters, the stream's lattice) - the old rule mis-stated 2.7% of inch records; the new rule miscounts none and refuses none in either unit. Refusals are reached only by records with many tiny rungs (e.g. 0.15 deep in rungs of 0.012, inch) or a lattice disagreement on the crest.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder.rs`:
- `g76_words_cut_exactly_the_records_passes_in_mm_and_inch` - parses the posted J/K as grid steps, counts ceil(K/J) and asserts it equals both the G33 pass count of the same document and ceil(height / first depth) of its record; asserts J is under one grid step over the record's first cut.
- `g76_refuses_by_name_when_no_grid_j_cuts_the_records_passes` - mm: crest +2 um (inside the lattice allowance) makes K 2.402, refused (J 0.801 would be a full step heavy); inch: 0.15 deep in 0.012 rungs, K 118 steps, no whole J with 12J < 118 <= 13J, refused.

Updated: `a_thread_posts_as_one_g76_block_with_the_option_in_mm_and_inch` (inch line J0.0315, golden regenerated).

Mutation checks (each mutation applied, suites run, file restored and touched):
- delete `if (j < lo) j = lo;` -> both new tests red (and the golden test);
- delete the refusal `return { why: ... }` line -> refusal test red;
- drop the `j <= hi` half of the refusal condition -> refusal test red (inch case);
- drop the `j - jRec < 1` half -> refusal test red (mm case).

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (post suites 5 s, app suites 1648 s - the shared golden pulled every app suite). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder --test lathe_post_tormach_thread -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised: a PathPilot / LinuxCNC run of the new inch golden; no batch gate (budget).

## Overlaps

- #517 and #518 (G76 on both lathe posts): `git merge-tree` with each branch is clean (#517 changes `g76Why`, this changes `g76Grid`), so not stacked. With #517's finish-allowance rule the record's rung count is still ceil(height / first depth).
- #1667 and #1681 conflict with this on adjacent lines of the same inch golden and `lathe_post_tormach_thread.rs` (their G30 / drive-line changes next to the G76 line): a mechanical keep-both, regenerate the golden at merge.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1619-g76-inch-ladder.md`.

Fork synced at v0.19.0 (branched from upstream/main 058e14ca).

Changelog: Tormach lathe G76 (inch) states a first depth J whose LinuxCNC R1 ladder cuts exactly the verified passes (J0.0315, not 0.0314, on the M12x2 fixture); a record no grid J can state is refused by name.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1619
